angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 8,406,143 km at 31.03 pc = 3.62 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75458: distance 31.027 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 31.027 +/- 0.093 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 32.5239 +/- 0.1310 mas (same row, RUWE 2.68), 248.3 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 12.083 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75458: radius 12.083 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 57.211 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.055) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 8,406,143 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4570 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75458: effective temperature 4570 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.064) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 75458: effective temperature 4570 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.064) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of iot Dra (pscomppars): spectral type K2 III, from Hill et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..211H/abstract)
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of iot Dra (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.03 dex, from Hill et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..211H/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of iot Dra (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 1.72247, from Hill et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..211H/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of iot Dra (pscomppars): age 2.65 Gyr, from Hill et al. 2021 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..211H/abstract)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 2.42 from 2024A&A...691A..53S; the 30 published values span log g 2.38 to 3.67, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.6% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024A%26A...691A..53S)
